bug_description.original: An out of bounds read occurs when searching for the tag message during tag parsing. The code uses `strstr(buffer, "\n\n")` to locate the separator between tag fields and the tag message, but since `strstr` does not accept a buffer length, it may read past the end of the buffer. This can result in `strstr` returning a pointer outside the buffer, causing the subsequent calculation of `buffer_end - buffer` to overflow and potentially lead to an invalid memory allocation.
bug_description.normalized:
When libgit2 parses the staged 73-byte raw tag object on the `GIT_OBJ_TAG` path, `git_tag__parse_raw` passes `tag_parse` a bounded span `[data, data + size)`. The witness ends with the single byte `' '` immediately after `tagger <>
`, so after the earlier tag fields are parsed the remaining span is only one byte long. `tag_parse` checks only `buffer < buffer_end` and `*buffer != '
'`, then calls `strstr(buffer, "

")` to look for the header/message separator. Because `strstr` expects a NUL-terminated string and ignores the explicit buffer length, it searches past the heap-backed fuzz input and AddressSanitizer reports a 2-byte heap-buffer-overflow READ at `src/tag.c:142`. The fix replaces this search with length-bounded `git__memmem(buffer, buffer_end - buffer, "

", 2)`.

source.description: First project-code step on the vulnerable path that consumes the attacker-controlled bytes and exact input length to establish the bounded tag-parser span.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 73-byte raw tag object later copied onto the heap by libFuzzer. On the `GIT_OBJ_TAG` iteration, `git_tag__parse_raw` receives that buffer as `data,size` and turns it into the parser bounds `[data, data + size)`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description:
The parser looks for `"

"` with `strstr` even though the remaining input is a bounded byte span, not a NUL-terminated C string. This ignores `buffer_end` and allows the search to read past the heap buffer when the separator is missing. The fix replaces this with `git__memmem(buffer, buffer_end - buffer, "

", 2)`.

sink.description: ASan sink. `strstr` starts at the last in-bounds byte of the heap-backed fuzz input and performs a 2-byte read while searching for `"\n\n"`, crossing `buffer_end` into the redzone.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled cursor is advanced through the `tagger <>\n` line and left on the lone trailing space byte at the end of the witness. That makes the remaining span `[buffer, buffer_end)` exactly one byte when the later message-separator search begins.

parser_admitted.description: During the `GIT_OBJ_TAG` iteration of the brute-force type loop, `def->parse_raw` resolves to `git_tag__parse_raw` and the raw witness enters the tag parser. The ASan stack confirms this dispatch path through `git_tag__parse_raw` and `tag_parse`.

fine_trace.note: On the `GIT_OBJ_TAG` dispatch path, the raw fuzz bytes and exact length are turned into the bounded span `[data, data + size)`. For the staged witness, `size` is 73, so every later in-bounds access must stay below `buffer_end = data + 73`.

fine_trace.code: search = memchr(buffer, '\n', buffer_end - buffer); ... buffer = search + 1;
fine_trace.note:
After `git_oid__parse` accepts the leading `object <40-hex>
` header and the fixed `type tag
` / `tag ` checks pass on the witness, `memchr` finds the newline ending the empty tag name and advances `buffer` to the next line. `buffer` now points at the attacker-controlled `tagger <>
` field.

The tagger-line guard is true because `buffer` points at `tagger <>\n`. `git_signature__parse` consumes that line up to the newline and updates `buffer` to the byte after it. In the witness that byte is the final trailing space, so only one byte remains: `buffer_end - buffer == 1`.

Message parsing is still entered because `buffer < buffer_end` and the sole remaining byte is `' '`, not `'
'`. No guard checks that the remaining span is large enough to hold the two-byte separator `"

"` or that the data is NUL-terminated before the search.

Root cause and ASan sink. `strstr` treats `buffer` as an unbounded C string and ignores `buffer_end`; with only one in-bounds non-NUL byte left and no in-range `"

"`, the search performs a 2-byte read across the end of the 73-byte heap-backed input. AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow` READ of size 2 at `src/tag.c:142`. The fix replaces this call with `git__memmem(buffer, buffer_end - buffer, "

", 2)`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation context is libFuzzer's heap copy of the same 73-byte witness span that step 1 turns into `[data, data + size)`; the project bug is the later unbounded search past that span in `tag_parse`.
